visualLanguage: design_system/public/PUBLIC_UI.md. Built from components/site/v3. No mockup in this directory: the place-type class is the city/community type-card landing, not a Tetherow one-off.
competitiveTarget: Beat Zillow / Redfin / Coldwell Banker type-filtered city results. Those surfaces dump the visitor into a search grid. This page is a place-type node: leftover count and median that already back the type card, a living atlas of the parent city with the type stated in the claim, and a photographed list of that type. Unique title, canonical, ItemList when listings exist. Breadcrumb is City then type, no Home.
note: H1 is `{Type} in {Place}` and it is the page's only display-scale line: the Atlas opens under the claim wearing an eyebrow (V3Atlas headlineTone='eyebrow', subject softened to Listings). One section-0 sourced claim sentence sits under the H1 — count and ~p90 price band from ONE listing_tile_mv read, worded as the address census with the map marking for-sale homes inside city limits (pending key hidden on this page). A V3Carousel mode=rail of photographed listings (PlaceTypeFilm; shadcn-carousel adapted with side prev/next) follows Atlas in the fold with price+address+beds/baths/sqft on 800x600 plates. The Atlas section is UNCONDITIONAL via PlaceTypeAtlasSection + PlaceTypeAtlasStandin. Rows and marks share one hovered key. Unknown type notFound(). Do not collide with app/cities/[slug]/[neighborhoodSlug].

tasteReview.beats: Redfin/Zillow's Bend neighborhood pages, on linkage: dragging the price histogram, tapping a map cluster, and paging the listing filmstrip all move the same marker and the same detail card here, where a portal makes you bounce between a separate list view, a separate map view, and a separate detail page to do the equivalent work.

defects.section: LISTINGS ON THE MAP cluster pills
defects.finding: every pill on the map reads 'N homes / $median' except one near the bottom-right cluster, which drops to a bare '$479k' with no count line, breaking the mark language the rest of the map teaches the reader in the first three seconds

the mobile dial view ends in a large blank cream field below the 3-visible-thumbnail filmstrip, dead space on the one viewport where scroll real estate is scarce, reading as an unfinished layout rather than a deliberate pause

defects.section: BD/BA/SQFT/$SQFT spec row + NEAR THIS PRICE comps list
defects.finding: a bare number-over-label spec grid with no sentence telling the reader what it means (a KPI grid), sitting above a comps list that states price deltas but never says whether that gap buys more house, less land, or a worse street — this block is interchangeable with any national portal's listing card

tasteReview.verdict: demoMatch is false: nothing on this page reproduces a named catalog demo, cream-box or otherwise — the map, the claim line, and the listing dial are all house-built, which is correct per the retired-carousel note but means the catalog UX bar was never actually cleared here. What's on screen is a competent, on-brand, MLS-honest listings summary with a genuinely linked map/histogram/dial interaction chain, but the card, spec row, and comps list are stock portal furniture (the KPI-grid tell) that a buyer would not screenshot to show a friend. It beats a static portal page on linkage and loses to nothing named in the taste brief on originality of form.
